description: Attack shape 7 (mixed1024 b60, ~107ms) -- the largest shape still wholly on cuSOLVER, highest idle on the board (17.3%). Its per-matrix syevd rest matrices are n=1024, above the cluster kmax 836, so they cannot use brief-56 peel-rest directly. Apply a matrix-sign D&C split (the brief-43/47 sign machinery already in the tree): shift + Newton-Schulz sign(A) -> two ~512-wide invariant-subspace blocks per matrix -> route those <=512 blocks through the existing batched cluster peel-rest path (mega_eigh_clust_split C=3 + NS2 orthonormalize + gate) -> membership rank-select -> reassemble. Collapses shape-7 rest per-matrix syevd into batched tensor-core work. Per-matrix residual-gated + cuSOLVER fallback.

Whole-batch single-level sign-DC-split for mixed1024 (shape 7): K=640 ns=30, reduced blocks via cluster-megakernel+NSx2, per-matrix gate+cuSOLVER fallback. Shape7 REGRESSED 107ms->200ms: nsys shows mega_eigh_clust_split_k=61ms (34.5%, the reduced-block cluster solve on 120 stacked K=640 blocks) dominates, plus ~25-52/60 unbalanced matrices fall back to cuSOLVER (paying both). Sign-split is heterogeneous (npos 223-683) so a fixed-K whole-batch split cannot cover it.

Peel router for mixed1024 (brief mechanism, 'peel structured first + sign-DC the dense rest'): two-level(5)->two-level path; dense-balanced PR[88,120)(28)->sign-DC-split K=640 cuSOLVER-reduced ns=30 (cluster-reduced MEASURED broken at n=1024: nbad 27/28 orth~3.6, the FP16-reduction eigenvectors too coarse for membership); rest(27)->cuSOLVER. Shape7 REGRESSED 107ms->153ms. Head-to-head on the 28 dense-balanced: sign-DC K=640 cuSOLVER-reduced=66.5ms vs low-rank k=608=36.0ms vs their cuSOLVER-marginal ~29ms. Sign-DC loses; peeling loses (cuSOLVER's whole-batch efficiency makes the ~29ms marginal < the 43ms peel cost). Shapes 4/5/6/10/11/12 UNCHANGED.

Peel with dense-balanced subset via LOW-RANK k=608 (the best fast path for it, 36ms standalone) instead of sign-DC, + two-level peel + cuSOLVER rest. Shape7 119ms (vs sign-DC 153ms, vs cuSOLVER 107ms) -- STILL a loss. Root cause quantified: cuSOLVER's whole-batch syevd marginal is ~0.85ms/matrix UNIFORM across ALL spectra (dense/steep/nearrank/mid/two-level all 0.79-0.90ms/mat), while every batched fast path has a fixed ~15-55ms floor that at these subset sizes exceeds the marginal (LR 28-dense=1.29ms/mat, two-level 5=1.3ms/mat). Peeling also DEGRADES the remaining cuSOLVER batch efficiency. Shapes 4/5/6/10/11/12 UNCHANGED.

Two-level-only peel for mixed1024 (dense peel disabled) + cuSOLVER rest. Shape7 110ms vs parent cuSOLVER 107ms (+3ms, within noise); nsys: span 111.4ms busy 90.1ms idle 19.1% 9211 kernels (parent 107.7/88.3/18.0%/8722). Isolates that even the 9x two-level win loses at the margin (5 two-level matrices: 6.5ms two-level-path vs 3.9ms cuSOLVER-marginal + gather/scatter). CONCLUSION of the peel sweep: peel-nothing==parent is the floor; every peel regresses. Shapes 4/5/6/10/11/12 unchanged. Reseed sweep (5 seeds) of the sign-DC-dense path: 0-1 fallback, 0 post-fallback harness-gate violations (safe, never wrong).

Explored brief-58 (sign-DC-split for shape-7 mixed1024, parent 6497c495a geomean 29789.5us). 4 trials, ALL regress; best 29862.6us (t4). Shape-7 measured facts: parent pure-cuSOLVER 107ms/60mat, busy 88ms + 18% idle (19.4ms) from ~3635 sub-10us launch gaps across 8722 kernels; whole-batch cuSOLVER marginal is ~0.85ms/matrix UNIFORM across ALL spectra (dense/steep/nearrank/mid/two-level 0.79-0.90ms/mat -- costmap probed). Sign-DC did NOT beat the per-matrix cuSOLVER loop, in any config: (t1) whole-batch K=640 ns=30 cluster+NS reduced -> 200ms (nsys: reduced-block cluster megakernel on 120 K=640 blocks = 61ms/34.5% + 25-52/60 unbalanced fall back paying both); (t2) peel two-level + sign-DC-the-dense-balanced-rest (K=640, cuSOLVER-reduced -- cluster-reduced MEASURED broken at n=1024: nbad 27/28, its FP16 eigenvectors too coarse for membership) -> 153ms; head-to-head on the 28 dense-balanced: sign-DC K640 cuSOLVER-reduced=66ms vs low-rank k608=36ms vs cuSOLVER-marginal ~25ms. NS_ITERS=30 is the load-bearing n=1024 fix (16 -> mass fallback even w/ exact reduced solver; found via probe). Sign-split is HETEROGENEOUS (n+ 223-683, maxside 522-801) so a fixed-K whole-batch split cannot cover it -- only the dense-balanced ~28 (maxside<=600) resolve. WHY peeling loses (the deeper finding): cuSOLVER's per-matrix marginal (~0.85ms) is below EVERY batched fast path's per-matrix cost at these subset sizes (LR dense 1.29ms/mat, two-level 1.3ms/mat), AND peeling degrades the remaining cuSOLVER batch's GPU efficiency (rest-27 costs 2.8ms/mat vs 0.85 in the full 60-batch). (t3) LR dense peel + two-level -> 119ms; (t4) two-level-ONLY peel -> 110ms (+3ms). The peel sweep limit is peel-nothing==parent. Correctness is SOLID: reseed sweep (5 seeds) of sign-DC-dense = 0-1 fallback, 0 post-fallback harness-gate violations; validate 39/39 every trial; shapes 4/5/6/10/11/12 UNCHANGED (routing guarded to n=1024 heterogeneous). OPEN directions: (1) the 18% idle (19.4ms, ~3635 launch gaps) is only reclaimable by a GENUINELY batched dense n=1024 eigensolver in ONE launch -- neither cluster megakernel (kmax 836) nor sign-DC achieves it accurately+fast; a fused n=1024 batched tridiag+Sturm+D&C megakernel (new large kernel, like the n<=448 mega extended out of SMEM via cluster-CTAs to n=1024) would target the idle directly. (2) reduce the ~0.85ms/mat cuSOLVER floor itself -- would need replacing syevd's per-matrix Householder+laed loop wholesale, not peeling. (3) sign-DC reduced-block accuracy: cluster-reduced fails at n=1024 (coarse FP16 eigenvectors); a batched reduced solver that is BOTH fast AND accurate at k~512-640 is the missing piece if sign-DC is revisited. All measured, none pursued further -- manager's call.
